<reason>Both sides built real, competing cases and both handled the Q&A format correctly (clear Q1/Q2, clear A1/A2 openings), with equal execution costs for clipped rebuttals. CON's strongest and most original move was the substitution/waterbed argument: flag the one auditable cost-recovery route and traffic moves to unauditable ingredient downgrades. It also landed a genuine hit by turning PRO's own patchwork (threshold, window, exemption, lineage) into a compliance manual, and by exploiting PRO's awkward concession that a relaunch "resets expectations honestly," i.e. exits the flag for free. But CON's foundational pillar — the information is already printed and shoppers ignore it — was materially damaged. PRO's level-versus-delta distinction (a per-100g figure is the arithmetic input, not a disclosure of change) was clean, and the "was £2.00, now £1.50" rebuttal was the sharpest stroke of the debate: the industry itself proves delta framing gets read, and abandons it only when the delta indicts the seller. CON's reply (promotions are dated and temporary; a permanent ledger would be a museum) mischaracterised a proposal that PRO had already limited to an event trigger and a defined window. CON also conceded that headline price rises are visible but then claimed "no gain," which is a category error PRO flagged: shifting cost recovery from an obscured route to a visible one is precisely the transparency win. CON's substitution claim also cuts both ways — if the flag stings enough to redirect behaviour, it is doing informational work. PRO's closing asymmetry (manufactured salience, deployed in one direction by the party controlling the label) crystallised the clash more decisively than CON's cost-migration ledger, which rested on that weak "no gain" link. Clear but competitive win for PRO.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's [A4.4]–[A4.5]: retailers already print "was £2.00, now £1.50," proving delta framing gets read — so CON's inattention defence is not consumer indifference but salience manufactured in one direction only. CON's "promotions are dated, a ledger of weights is a museum" reply strawmanned PRO's event-triggered, windowed flag and left that pillar damaged.</best_rebuttal>
